content: Cross-session message held by the receiving session (recipient: @cc-review19-held). Claude in that session hasn't seen it. The usual cause is that the two sessions are in different permission modes: a terminal session then asks for approval there, but the desktop app and non-interactive sessions can't ask, so there the message expires undelivered unless the modes come to match. A session can also be set to hold every message.

content.text:
The message to `cc-review19-held` was sent but has not been delivered. The session is holding it, most likely because its permission mode differs from this one. Its Claude hasn't seen the message.

I'm not resending, since a resend would only add to the hold. Another notice will arrive if the hold is released, denied, or expires. If the message needs to get through, the two sessions' permission modes may need to match, or someone may need to approve it in that session.
